title: Otis and the Glowing Plum
markdown:
Otis the duck loved mornings. He loved the way soft warm sunshine gently warmed his little bill, and the cheerful quacks of friends stirring from slumber. Most of all he loved waiting for the very first plum of the season to glow. A special plum: when it glowed, it was perfectly ripe and ready for tasting. He waddled, happy wobble, to the old plum tree, home of Plum, the little plum-tree pixie. Plum was always busy. Today she was carefully polishing her shimmering wings until they sparkled like captured moonlight.

“Hello there, my dear Otis,” she giggled, voice like tiny bells. She sprinkled petal dust from a nearby blossom onto her nose, which made her sneeze a very musical sound. “Ready to watch for the Wonderful, the Magical, the Very First Plum?”

Otis bounced his fluffy honey-coloured tail feathers. “Oh yes, Plum. I don’t think I’ve ever been more ready.”

They settled at the base of the tall tree, eyes wide and hopeful, gazing up into the leafy branches. Many little green plums still growing and waiting. They were patiently anticipating the one special plum that would glow with a warm light and whisper: I am perfectly ripe and ready to be tasted. Waiting for a beautiful secret from the afternoon sun.

Then, with a tiny soft movement, a little plum on the very highest branch began to shimmer. Not just any shimmer. A soft golden light, warm as a sleepy sunbeam that had decided to linger. Otis let out a happy little quack. “Look, Plum. It’s glowing. It’s really glowing.”

So gently the glowing plum gave a little sway, and as softly as a whisper it lifted from its stem. It did not fall. It floated away, as graceful as a tiny glowing balloon on a whisper of breeze.

“Oh my.” Otis’s eyes wide. “It’s floating away.”

Plum fluttered dewdropped wings. “My goodness. It’s never done that before. Let’s follow it.”

Otis looked at the little stream meandering past the tree. “How will we follow a plum that’s floating on its own?”

Plum, eyes twinkling, pointed to a large fallen leaf near the water. Just right. “We’ll make a boat.”

With a gentle nudge from Otis and careful guidance from Plum, the leaf eased into the stream. Otis settled on it, wobbly duck legs finding balance. Plum perched on the very edge, tiny feet barely making a ripple. The leaf boat bobbed, a gentle vessel.

“Welcome aboard,” said Plum. “Our journey to the glowing plum.”

The stream flowed like a ribbon of liquid moonlight, unhurried and ever so slow. Otis gently moved his webbed feet, helping their leaf drift along, while Plum, with a tiny twig, softly guided them. They drifted past tall slender reeds that seemed to whisper secrets to the soft passing breeze, and they watched as little silvery fish peeked out shyly from beneath smooth rounded stones. A dragonfly used the leaf’s wake as a road. And there, just ahead, they could still see the glowing plum, bobbing on the water, leading them gently onward. It felt like a special discovery, the kind you do not rush or you lose the glow.

After a while the narrow stream widened into a calm still pool, a shimmering mirror. The glowing plum waited just beyond a small bend, nestled among smooth pebbles at the edge of a quiet moss. It was still a plum, warm and gold, as if it had found the perfect place to rest. The water kept a ring of light around it, the kind you do not rush or you lose the glow.

They guided the leaf to the mossy bank. Plum moved ashore and, with the most tender touch, picked up the plum. Warm and smooth in her tiny hands. A wonderfully gentle journey, full of lovely discoveries.

“It’s absolutely perfect,” she whispered, and offered it to Otis. “After you, my very best friend.”

Otis leaned in and took a sweet soft bite. The plum was so sweet and wonderfully smooth. Sunshine mixed with the happiest thoughts. The most delicious plum he had ever tasted, warm as a pocket of afternoon. Plum took a bite too. They closed their eyes a moment, savouring, while the moss held the leftover gold.

As the sun began its slow descent, painting pink, lavender, and warm orange, they knew it was time to head home. They guided the leaf boat back along the stream, the sweet taste lingering like a soft memory.

At the familiar welcoming tree, Otis gave Plum a gentle nuzzle with his beak. “Thank you for the most wonderful journey.”

“Thank you, Otis.” She fluttered a little sleepily. “The glowiest plum journey I could have imagined.”

Otis waddled to his cozy nest among the reeds. He snuggled down, safe and warm. The moon peeked from behind a fluffy cloud, silvery glow. He thought of the magical plum, the leaf boat, and his friend Plum. A very special gentle day. Soon, like the plum finding its moss, he drifted into deep peaceful sleep, dreams of sweet fruit, quiet streams, and happy smiles, the taste still on his bill.
